steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere and shorter wavelengths of light (blue) are scattered much more effectively than longer wavelengths (red and orange). As sunlight enters the atmosphere, blue light is scattered in all directions across the sky, making the entire sky appear blue to an observer on the ground. At sunrise and sunset, light travels through more of the atmosphere, scattering away most of the blue light and leaving the longer red and orange wavelengths to dominate the colors we see.
